title: CVA assurance report
description: The named PS §2.3 deliverable. Versioned $id plus a schema_version on every instance: a report that cannot be re-read next month is not the 'reproducible audit log' PS §2.3 asks for. Module E's dashboard is a SECOND CONSUMER of this same file and never recomputes a disposition, confidence or coverage row.

scan_id.description: VOLATILE (§5.3). One grammar, two producers: a per-day counter normally, and the last 4 digits of sha256(seed) under --profile selftest. Module E validates this as a path segment and refuses anything else, so the selftest form has to match the same regex.

created_at_utc.description: VOLATILE (§5.3). Pinned to a frozen clock under --profile selftest.

target.description: What was scanned. Absent members are absent facts, not empty strings.

arch_hash.description: sha256 over the model's STRUCTURE (module/op types and parameter shapes), never its weights. Absent for a query-only model, which has no structure to read.

preprocess_hash.description: sha256 of the JCS canonical form of the DECLARED preprocessing spec after quantisation (mean/std/value_range as floor(x*1e6+0.5) integers). Absent when the operator declared no spec.

preprocess_ref.description: The bare content-addressed name (<preprocess_hash>.json) of the stored quantised spec in the shared evidence store, so prov.recompute can re-run it.

model_opset.description: READ from the model and recorded, never gated: ONNX Runtime accepts opset 7+ and a gate would reject valid models.

access_assumptions.description: PS §2.2.2 requires access assumptions PER ASSESSMENT; this is the scan-level header that §7.4 prints, and each Finding carries its own list as well.

capabilities_absent.description: Every absence carries a REASON. 'Gradients NOT AVAILABLE' alone is not an access assumption; 'onnxruntime-training not bundled (declared narrowing, ADR-001)' is.

plan.description: Resolved and printed BEFORE any work starts — coverage is known at minute zero. All four states print at equal prominence; a shorter report must never look like a cleaner result.

contributor_risk.description: PS §2.2.1's source-level aggregation. Rendered BEFORE individual findings: it is what an acceptance analyst acts on. A beta-binomial posterior, never a raw flag rate — 3/5 = 60% must not outrank 800/10000 = 8%.

excludes_cohort_rate.description: ci_low is above this group's cohort rate: the flag rate of the OTHER non-outlier groups, so a group never informs its own baseline.

excludes_reference_rate.description: Present only when a reference dataset was usable: ci_low is above the upper 95% bound of the reference dataset's flag rate. Informational; D4 stays keyed on excludes_cohort_rate.

contributor_baseline.description: B7's absolute rate against a reference clean set: a SECOND dataset the operator supplies with `--reference-dataset`, run through the same data checks. It guards the cohort prior's blind spot: a cohort contaminated as a whole, where no contributor stands out. null when none was supplied, or when it was supplied but unusable (then contributor_baseline_unavailable says why). The reference's findings appear nowhere else in this report.

reference_flagged.description: of those, sample-level findings that ran and were routed to review or quarantine: the same definition of 'flagged' the cohort uses

reference_rate_ci_high.description: upper end of the 95% Jeffreys interval on reference_rate; what the cohort is compared to, since a reference that flagged nothing does not show a true rate of zero

cohort_rate.description: the scanned dataset's robust cohort rate: the flag rate of its groups after upper-tail outlier groups are set aside (first grouping key with data)

cohort_exceeds_reference.description: cohort_rate is above reference_rate_ci_high: the cohort prior is unreliable here, because the baseline every group is compared with is itself dirtier than clean data

contributor_baseline_unavailable.description: Present only when a reference dataset was supplied but its flag rate could not be computed (over the embedding ceiling, no embedding index, a check raised, or nothing to run). Never present when none was supplied.

permutation_test.description: Mandatory at B7: are flags non-randomly distributed across groups AT ALL? This is the Sybil case the cohort prior structurally cannot see.

provenance_summary.description: Printed EVEN WHEN NOTHING FAILED (Module C open item O9). System-Overview says Module C 'only enters the report on failure', which is right about FINDINGS and wrong about the SECTION: a report with no provenance section is indistinguishable from a scan where provenance was never checked. Absence of evidence must not render as evidence of absence.

calibration.description: The system's own confidence is evidence, and evidence gets shown — so the reliability diagram and Brier score live INSIDE the coverage statement, not in an appendix.

scored_on.description: How `brier` and `reliability_bins` were measured. `out_of_fold` means every prediction scored here came from a curve fitted without the point it predicted — the only basis on which a reliability diagram may be read as a quality claim. `none` means the fit had no second group to hold out, so no score is reported rather than an in-sample one presented as held out.

calibrated_detectors.description: The detector ids a calibrator was actually fitted for. Everything else in the report carries its detector's OWN raw score, and the disposition table's confidence thresholds (D3, D5) are not applied to those findings — they route on severity alone and are capped at review. Without this list a reader cannot tell which confidences are on the calibrated scale.

excluded_detectors.description: prov.* bypass calibration entirely: a hash mismatch is arithmetic, not a belief. Fitting a curve to a deterministic check produces a calibrated probability on a certainty, and feeding a degenerate class to the isotonic fit corrupts it for every other detector.

coverage.description: GENERATED by walking the registry's attack_class/requires declarations — never hand-assembled. PS §2.2.5's explicit non-coverage statement.

counts_only_kind.description: operational classes are true reports about the system's own state, not attack classes we claim to detect; counting them would inflate the statement with things no attacker does.

reproduction.description: PS §2.3's reproducible audit log. DECLARING THE VOLATILE SET IS THE DELIVERABLE (§5.3) — 'byte-identical twice' is impossible as stated, because scan_id and created_at_utc are volatile by design, and an auditor needs to know which fields are expected to differ rather than be handed an assertion that cannot hold.

volatile_paths.description: JSON PATHS, not bare field names: scan_id is on the report AND on every finding, so a top-level deletion is not enough and the diff must walk the tree.

path.description: The BARE CONTENT HASH, resolved against the shared <out_dir>/evidence/. Never scan_id-prefixed: that would smuggle the volatile field back into every finding.

data.description: In-memory payload; transport, not the record. Materialised into the store and hashed at write time.

finding_id.description: sha256(detector_id‖detector_version‖target_type‖target_ref‖attack_class)[:16] — SCAN-INVARIANT. If it hashed scan_id, every finding would be volatile and the reproducibility diff would be worthless.

reason.description: Must NAME THE EVIDENCE, not just a score. 'Suspicious sample (score 0.87)' is a number wearing a finding's clothes; if a template cannot be written in the evidential style, the detector should emit info severity.

attack_class.description: Must be declared in core/taxonomy.py — an undeclared string makes the coverage row silently vanish.

disposition_rule.description: WHICH rule fired — 'why this disposition?' always has a specific answer.
